title: Streaming consumer contracts and checkpointed retry UX for Python SDK
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: Customers building low-latency chat experiences need a Python SDK that makes streaming completions feel 'native' in applications: easy to consume, resilient to transient network errors, and capable of resuming without duplicate application-level side effects. The existing callback-centric API has proven hard to compose with asyncio patterns and harder to reason about for exactly-once semantics when downstream side effects (DB writes, message enqueues) are involved.

Goal: Design and implement a new consumer contract for the Python SDK that: (1) provides a unified sync/async iterable/iterator surface for streaming chat events, (2) exposes lightweight, application-visible checkpoint tokens to enable idempotent resume and at-least-once delivery control, (3) integrates a pluggable retry & backpressure policy that cooperates with asyncio event loop scheduling, and (4) ships clear examples and migration guidance from the older callback API.

Scope: This ticket covers API design, prototype implementation, test harnesses (simulated network glitches, reorder/dup events), example notebooks, and docs. It intentionally excludes TypeScript/Go SDKs (coordination ticket created), server/runtime changes (only backward-compatible protocol adjustments will be requested), and dedicated console UI work.
acceptance_criteria: New Python streaming consumer provides both async iterator and synchronous iterator wrappers with consistent event typing
SDK emits a compact checkpoint token (opaque string) at deterministic safe points that callers can persist and pass back to resume streams
Resume semantics demonstrated: resumed stream continues from last application-acknowledged checkpoint without replaying acknowledged messages
Built-in retry policy supports exponential backoff, jitter, and a mode that converts transient errors into resumable tokens for later retry
Examples and migration guide added: one asyncio chat server example, one Flask (sync) example, and a short snippet showing migration from callback-based code
Unit and integration tests cover network interruption, duplicate events, and consumer-side backpressure behavior
Telemetry spans emitted for start/resume/complete/failure and expose token IDs for tracing correlation
Docs and API surface reviewed and approved by SDK PM and lead of Infrastructure (comments resolved)
comments: 2025-02-15 - Ava Martinez: Created initial ticket after sync with PM (Ishaan) and two client teams requesting resumable streaming. Draft design attached.

2025-02-18 - Jason Li: Spike completed — prototype implements async iterator with 'checkpoint_token' yielded on 'commit' signal. Opened prototype PR for feedback: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/4123
2025-02-19 - Design review (Sofia Kim): prefer opaque token vs numeric offsets to allow protocol freedom. Also requested clearer ergonomics for sync users. Assigned small design follow-up.
2025-02-21 - PM feedback (Ishaan Patel): prioritize migration example and docs; mark customer_impact=medium. Also suggested exposing retry hooks for advanced users.
2025-02-23 - Jason Li: Implemented retry policy pluggable interface and added default AsyncExponentialRetry. Added unit tests simulating socket reset and JSON chunk truncation.

2025-02-24 - QA (Rhea Gupta): Integration test failing intermittently under heavy backpressure; investigating event loop scheduling interactions. Possible fix: yield-to-loop in consumer and small buffer window tuning.
2025-02-26 - Jason Li: Resolved backpressure issue by exposing 'max_inflight_events' and integrating with asyncio.Queue with backpressure-aware put. Tests stabilised.
2025-02-27 - Security (Nish): quick review — opaque tokens must not embed PII. Confirmed; tokens are HMAC-signed server-side and client only stores opaque string (doc updated).

2025-02-28 - Jason Li: Changes merged to main in draft release branch. Docs PR opened: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Streaming+Consumer+Contracts. Next: add migration guide and example notebooks; coordinate with TS SDK owner to align surface.
